content.user_title: Diagnose and Fix CI Failures Safely
content.value_statement: CI failures can hide the root cause behind long logs and recent changes. This skill guides structured analysis and safe fixes without disabling tests or quality checks.
actual_capabilities: Classifies CI failures as build, test, dependency, or environment issues.
Guides retrieval and review of GitHub Actions failure logs with the GitHub CLI.
Suggests root-cause-focused fixes for failing tests and implementation defects.
Uses Git history commands to connect recent changes with a failure.
Requests approval before changing tests or CI settings when implementation is not clearly at fault.
Recommends rerunning focused and full test suites after a fix.
limitations: It requires access to CI logs and the relevant repository to diagnose a specific failure.
It cannot determine product requirements when tests and implementation disagree.
It does not replace project-specific CI configuration or maintainer review.
It may need installed GitHub CLI and project test dependencies for command-based investigation.

use_cases.title: Investigate a failed pull request check
use_cases.description: Review a failed CI job, isolate the first error, and propose the next safe action.

use_cases.title: Repair a failing automated test
use_cases.description: Classify an assertion, timeout, type, or mock failure and validate a focused fix.

use_cases.title: Trace a regression after recent changes
use_cases.description: Use structured Git history to identify commits and files likely connected to a pipeline failure.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a CI failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this CI failure log and identify the first likely root cause. Explain the next safe step.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a failing test
prompt_templates.prompt: The CI test fails with this error: [paste error]. Review the test and implementation. Propose a root-cause fix without skipping or weakening the test.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a regression
prompt_templates.prompt: CI started failing after recent commits. Use the failure log and Git history to identify likely responsible changes and provide a verification plan.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an approved CI change
prompt_templates.prompt: The test expectation or CI setting may be outdated. Prepare an approval request that states the reason, proposed change, alternatives, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Analyze a CI log showing a TypeScript error.
output: Likely cause: a recent API change does not match the declared type.
Next steps: inspect the referenced file, correct the type or implementation, then rerun the focused build.

output_examples.input: A test times out in CI but passes locally.
output: Possible cause: CI timing or an unresolved asynchronous operation.
Next steps: inspect awaited work and environment differences, then rerun the target test and full suite.

best_practices: Start with the first meaningful error in the CI log before addressing downstream failures.
Compare test behavior with product requirements before changing a test expectation.
Run the focused test first, then run the full suite to check for regressions.
anti_patterns: Do not skip tests, remove assertions, or use CI bypasses to make a pipeline pass.
Do not change tests or CI settings without explicit approval when requirements are unclear.
Do not diagnose a failure from the final log line alone when earlier errors exist.

faq.question: What failures can this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It covers build, test, dependency, and environment failures in CI and CD pipelines.

faq.question: Can it work with GitHub Actions?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents GitHub CLI commands for listing runs and viewing failed logs.

faq.question: Will it disable a failing test?
faq.answer: No. It explicitly discourages skips, removed assertions, and CI bypasses.

faq.question: Can it modify a test?
faq.answer: It can guide a test correction when the implementation is correct, but unclear changes require user approval.

faq.question: How does it identify regressions?
faq.answer: It can use structured Git history and changed-file information to connect recent commits with failures.

faq.question: What should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide the failed job log, the failing test name if available, and relevant recent changes.
